text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; you mentioned a history of delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and bone fragility. To start our evaluation, please describe in detail what those unusual physical features look like and when they first appeared.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency (Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia)

The combination of ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly, labial fusion) at birth, hypertension-related maternal hair growth during pregnancy, and severe acne suggests a defect in cortisol and estrogen synthesis with excess androgen production. I will confirm this by requesting hormone levels and imaging. REQUEST TEST: Plasma_17-hydroxyprogesterone, Renin, Aldosterone, Cortisol; REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.
